note: [agent-bulk] shw 14003 (312.3 MeV, pdg 11, 7 segments) is the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 shower (correction 17) and the highest-energy object in the event; no non-EM object was passed over. It is the textbook nuecc electron: it starts ON the nu vertex (closest member point distV 0.0), runs ~40 cm as a narrow MIP stem, then opens into a branching fan out to 61.6 cm -- visible as stem-then-fan in BOTH shower azimuths (az-055 and az+085), so the cone is 3-D and not a projection artifact, and the member skeleton gives extent 42.5 cm with transverse RMS 5.06 cm (2*RMS/L = 0.24) after dropping the far 0.2 cm fragment. Members 14001/14003/14006/14007/14008 are all cluster 14 and mutually touching (gaps 0.0-8.3 cm). Nothing contiguous is missing: the ONLY substantial grey/unowned segment in the event is 14004 (19.6 cm, pdg 13) and it leaves the vertex at 89.8deg to the shower seed's direction -- the second prong of a clean two-prong vertex, correctly left unowned. Every other non-member is the seed of its own sub-20 MeV shower (correction 16) and none is contiguous: the nearest, 42017 (11.3 MeV, 2.2 cm) at 40.5 cm / 72.4deg, is 22.8 cm from the closest member; 57032 (21.6 MeV, 0.8 cm) at 59.8 cm / 35.8deg is 37.2 cm away. Weak over-clustering item I did NOT record and would let the owner reverse: 52027 (0.2 cm, pdg 13) is a member at 61.6 cm from the vertex with a 33.1 cm gap to the nearest other member -- a 2-point fragment carrying essentially no charge, taken far out on axis. Showers NOT looked at individually: the 24 the scope rule skipped, all <= 11.3 MeV (42017 11.3, 24010 10.6, 45020 4.3, 48023 2.9, then 20 more under 2.9 down to 0.0). Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 99.3 cm half-span (r95 = 79.4 cm, below the 150 cm trigger, so no vtxz-* frames): in vtx-az+065-el+20 the star sits exactly at the fork of the electron stem and 14004; not vertex-bad. PI0: there is NO reco pi0 group (both pio_id = -1), so the pio-*.png frames are the capture's auto-slotted top two, NOT a reconstruction pairing (correction 3). That auto pair 14003+57032 prices at 132.3 MeV on the axis convention -- inside the code's accept window -- and I explicitly do NOT propose it: 14003 starts on the nu vertex so it cannot be a converted photon, the asymmetry is 0.87, and the vertex convention returns no chord. The separate kine_pio_* BDT block (mass 99.0, E2 11.3 MeV) does not even close with itself (70.2 vs 99.0) and is not a pairing either. GATE observation, same family as the one on evt396037 in this shard: no same-distance angle inversion here, but 14007 was accepted at 35.8 cm / 35.7deg -- well ABOVE the 25deg pass-1 line on the acceptance plot -- by site in_main_cluster, i.e. on cluster membership, while 57032 at essentially the same angle (35.8deg) but 59.8 cm out was rejected. Twice in this shard the accept/reject boundary is set by which cluster a segment is in rather than by the dist/angle gate.
